issues.justification: 'Тики-так' is thieves' slang for 'OK/fine/all right'. The English 'tick-tock' reads as a clock sound and is meaningless in context. It also breaks the jargon-lesson scene, where it is supposed to be the gloss for 'good', and the later 'Fine! I mean, tick-tock' gag. An English slang equivalent such as 'copacetic' or 'A-OK' would work.

issues.source_quote: Хороший человек? Забыл! Фрей-фея, действительно: Фрей-фея.
issues.translation_quote: A good person? Forgot! A mark... of course: a mark.
issues.justification: The joke is that the character half-recalls and mangles the slang word 'фраер' as 'фрей-фея'. The English 'mark... a mark' has no mangling or comic misremembering, and 'mark' is not an equivalent of 'a good person' in this exercise. The humor is lost.

The abbreviation is left untranslated and unexplained, so the English viewer cannot get the gag about Soviet anti-embezzlement police. It is also unclear why the speaker says it right after the English lesson.
'Не с чем' means 'there's nothing to congratulate me on'. 'Don't.' is too curt and does not convey that the capture was pointless without the helmet.

issues.source_quote: Все! Кина не будет. Электричество кончилось.
issues.translation_quote: That's it! No movie today. The electricity's run out.
issues.justification: 'Кина не будет' is a famous comic catchphrase with a folksy, jokey tone. The flat 'No movie today' loses that flavor, and 'The electricity's run out' is slightly unnatural.

This is a culturally specific reference (a well-known film and song title) that is transliterated without any adaptation. The target audience will not grasp the allusion or the comparison of the characters standing out in the open.

issues.translation_quote: All you ever do is croak doom.
issues.justification: 'Croak doom' is an unidiomatic literal rendering. Natural English would be 'All you do is prophesy doom' or 'You're a real prophet of doom'.

issues.source_quote: Вы Ваши 20 рублей положите в эту тумбочку, а на двери замок повесьте.
issues.translation_quote: Put your 20 rubles in this cabinet, and hang a padlock on the door.
issues.justification: The Russian is a direct instruction with a bedside-table detail. 'Cabinet' is imprecise, and the overall rendering is stiff for a spoken scheme explained to a colleague.
The reference to Chukovsky's villain Barmaley is left unexplained, so the cover-story joke about a villain-costume contest is weakened for English viewers.
